vignette: Juan is a 25-year-old Latin American man who works as a data scientist in a bustling tech company. He presents with symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder following the recent hospitalization and near-death experience of his young nephew, Diego. Juan has felt a deep sense of responsibility for Diego's health since his sister, Diego's mother, passed away from cancer two years ago. Juan vividly recalls the night he received the call that Diego had fallen ill with pneumonia that rapidly progressed to sepsis, requiring intensive care at the local hospital. Since then, Juan finds himself often re-experiencing that night through intrusive memories and nightmares where he hears his sister's voice pleading for help before transitioning into screams of fear and pain as if it were happening all over again. The intensity of these experiences is so overwhelming that they often leave him drenched in sweat, heart pounding, and feeling an intense urge to run out the door and check on Diego, even though he lives several hours away. At work, Juan struggles to concentrate on his data analyses; the numbers blur together, replaced by images of ICU machines beeping frantically. He is hyper-vigilant for any news from the hospital and often checks his phone obsessively, sometimes leaving meetings early in anticipation of a call. His anxiety spikes when he sees anything related to hospitals or illnesses, like advertisements for flu shots, causing him to feel dizzy and nauseous. Outside of work, Juan has started isolating himself from friends and social events that once brought him joy. He avoids going to the park where Diego used to play because it triggers memories of his last visit with his nephew before he fell ill. Conversations about children or medical emergencies are particularly distressing, leading him to steer clear of any related discussions. Juan's sleep has been severely disrupted since the incident; he rarely gets more than a few hours of restful sleep each night. When he does manage to fall asleep, it is frequently interrupted by nightmares where Diego's condition worsens despite Juan's frantic attempts to save him. Upon waking from these nightmares, Juan often feels paralyzed with fear and an overwhelming sense of helplessness. His appetite has also been affected; some days he finds himself barely eating, unable to taste or enjoy any food, while other days he craves comfort foods in excess, as if trying to numb the emotional pain through physical satiation. His body aches from the constant tension and his muscles feel perpetually tight, especially when he thinks about Diego's illness. On the weekends, Juan sometimes drives out of habit towards the hospital only to find himself lost in thought, unable to fully articulate why he is there or how he can be of help beyond being a concerned uncle. He feels guilty for not being able to prevent Diego's illness and struggles with survivor's guilt, wondering if he could have done more to protect his nephew. Despite these challenges, Juan continues to work diligently at his job as a data scientist, using the structured tasks and clear objectives as an anchor in his daily life. The routine of work offers him some sense of control amidst the chaos of his personal life. However, even here, he often feels disconnected from colleagues during social interactions, finding it difficult to engage fully without feeling consumed by thoughts about Diego's condition. Juan has started to seek solace in prayer and reflection, practices passed down through generations in his family. He spends time reading books and listening to music that reminds him of happier times with his sister and nephew, though these activities sometimes lead to a flood of emotions he is not prepared to face. Despite his efforts, Juan finds himself grappling daily with the fear and uncertainty that have become intertwined with his life since Diego's illness. His days are marked by a constant cycle of re-experiencing trauma through memories and nightmares, hyper-vigilance for any signs of bad news, avoidance of triggers, disrupted sleep patterns, and emotional numbing. Juan is navigating these challenges while trying to maintain his professional responsibilities and personal commitments.
